headline: Magna Carta Bill Seeks Stronger Protection for Waste Workers
seoTitle: Magna Carta Bill Seeks Waste-Worker Protections
seoDescription: Senate Bill No. 162 seeks fair compensation, hazard and emergency pay, social protection, health and safety measures, and protective equipment for waste workers.
deck: Senate Bill No. 162 seeks fair compensation, hazard and emergency pay, social protection, health and safety measures, and protective equipment for waste workers.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Senator Loren Legarda renewed her push for Senate Bill No. 162, the proposed Magna Carta of Waste Workers, which she refiled in the 20th Congress.

The proposal would establish safeguards for government, private-sector and informal waste workers through fair compensation, hazard and emergency pay, health and safety measures, access to social protection and appropriate protective equipment.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Legarda said an estimated 1.8 million to 2.3 million waste pickers and waste workers are in the Philippines, many of them informal, unregistered or unaccounted for.

The bill would guarantee key labor rights for private-sector workers, provide additional assistance for qualified government workers and formally recognize informal waste-worker organizations so they can access government support and representation.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Waste workers face exposure to hazardous materials, unstable employment and gaps in social protection while providing an essential public-health and environmental service. The proposal would place formal obligations behind protections that many workers currently lack.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The measure is a bill, not an enacted law. Watch for committee hearings, amendments, budget implications and action by both chambers of Congress.
